item.title: Attorney General Davenport Sues to Protect Housing Assistance for Families With Mixed Immigration Status
item.dc:creator: NJOAG Communications WC
item.category: Protecting NJ From Attacks Out Of DC
U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)
item.description:
Attorney General Jennifer Davenport joined 21 other attorneys general and the governor of Pennsylvania in challenging a new U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) rule that would strip federal housing assistance from families with mixed immigration status.

The post Attorney General Davenport Sues to Protect Housing Assistance for Families With Mixed Immigration Status appeared first on New Jersey Office of Attorney General.
item.content:encoded:
For Immediate Release: November 23, 2026

Office of the Attorney General
– Jennifer Davenport, Attorney General

For Further Information:

Media Inquiries-
Allison Inserro
OAGpress@njoag.gov

View Complaint

TRENTON — Attorney General Jennifer Davenport today joined 21 other attorneys general and the governor of Pennsylvania in challenging a new U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) rule that would strip federal housing assistance from families with mixed immigration status. Under the new rule, any eligible person, including a U.S. citizen, who shares a household with a non-U.S. citizen or ineligible immigrant would be cut off from HUD assistance entirely. The rule would also require all U.S. citizens in federal housing programs to prove their citizenship or risk eviction.

In a lawsuit filed in the U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts, Attorney General Davenport and the coalition argue that the rule illegally reverses nearly 30 years of federal law and policy allowing mixed-status families to stay together. They also argue it violates the Administrative Procedure Act (APA) by exceeding HUD’s authority to enact this arbitrary new restriction.

“This unnecessary and heartless rule will put children on the street,” said Attorney General Davenport. “Families should not have to choose between staying together or keeping a roof over their heads—and Congress did not impose that choice on families. HUD is straying beyond its authority to implement housing programs in the way Congress has directed.”

For nearly 30 years, federal housing programs have provided housing assistance to low-income families even if not every household member is eligible for assistance. If every household member is not eligible for assistance, HUD reduces the family’s subsidy so it covers only the eligible household members. Congress codified this protection in 1997, explicitly stating that families receiving prorated assistance “shall not” lose their benefits just because an ineligible family member lives with them.

The new HUD rule effectively eliminates this protection. Under the rule, a family can stay in HUD-assisted housing only if every household member is a U.S. citizen or an eligible immigrant. As a result, U.S. citizens and eligible immigrants who live with an ineligible relative will be forced to choose between maintaining their housing and keeping their family together.

HUD estimates that around 20,000 mixed-status families, totaling 78,100 people, will lose their housing assistance. This includes 55,000 people who are fully eligible for federal housing assistance, many of whom are children and seniors. The agency also acknowledges that the rule will lead to evictions and displacement, and that many of these families could become homeless.

The rule would also make it harder for millions of U.S. citizens to keep the housing they already qualify for. Under the new rule, every U.S. citizen would also need to provide their Social Security number and consent to have their citizenship status checked through the federal SAVE database. If SAVE cannot automatically confirm their citizenship, U.S. citizens would have to produce official documents to prove their status, such as an original or certified birth certificate, naturalization certificate, or passport. Nationwide, an estimated 3.8 million adult U.S. citizens lack a document proving their citizenship, and another 17.5 million face barriers to getting one.

The coalition asserts that the rule will increase homelessness and shift major costs onto state and local governments. By HUD’s own estimates, sheltering people displaced by the rule could cost governments between $20,000 and $50,000 per affected person each year. The rule would also shrink the supply of affordable housing more broadly. HUD acknowledges that losing rental assistance could leave many subsidized units vacant, reduce rental income for housing providers, and drive private landlords out of the Section 8 voucher program, making it even harder for eligible families to find a home.

Attorney General Davenport and the coalition argue that HUD’s new rule exceeds the agency’s authority and violates federal law, which expressly allows prorated assistance for mixed-status families and establishes different documentation requirements for U.S. citizens and eligible immigrants aged 62 and older. They argue that HUD also violated the APA by issuing an arbitrary and capricious rule. The coalition is asking the court to declare the rule unlawful, strike it down, and block HUD from implementing or enforcing it against the plaintiff states, their local governments, and their public housing authorities.

Joining Attorney General Davenport in filing this lawsuit, which is led by the attorneys general of New York, California, and Massachusetts, are the attorneys general of Arizona, Colorado, Connecticut, Delaware, Hawaii, Illinois, Maine, Maryland, Michigan, Minnesota, New Mexico, Oregon, Rhode Island, Virginia, Vermont, Washington, Wisconsin, and the District of Columbia, as well as the governor of Pennsylvania.

###

item.title: AG Davenport, Roxbury Township Ask Court to Stop ICE From Violating a Court Order and Moving Forward With Warehouse Work
item.dc:creator: NJOAG Communications WC
item.category: Protecting NJ From Attacks Out Of DC
item.description:
Attorney General Jennifer Davenport and the Township of Roxbury asked a federal district court to stop ICE from violating a court order that bars the Trump Administration from undertaking any work to convert a warehouse to a large-scale immigration detention center unless an environmental assessment is completed.

The post AG Davenport, Roxbury Township Ask Court to Stop ICE From Violating a Court Order and Moving Forward With Warehouse Work appeared first on New Jersey Office of Attorney General.
item.content:encoded:
ICE, DHS Are Violating Court Order by Issuing Construction Contract

For Immediate Release: November 23, 2026

Office of the Attorney General
– Jennifer Davenport, Attorney General

For Further Information:

Media Inquiries-
Allison Inserro
OAGpress@njoag.gov

View Motion to Enforce

TRENTON — Attorney General Jennifer Davenport and the Township of Roxbury today asked a federal district court to stop U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) from violating a court order that bars the Trump Administration from undertaking any work to convert a warehouse to a large-scale immigration detention center unless an environmental assessment is completed.

Attorney General Davenport and Roxbury filed today’s motion to enforce the court’s order after discovering that ICE and the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) awarded a construction contract valued at nearly $1 billion and intends to begin the project to convert the warehouse into a detention center.

The motion to enforce seeks to block the federal government from conducting construction work on the site, cancel any funding committed to construction work, and provide State and Roxbury officials an opportunity to inspect the site to ensure compliance, “Trump’s ICE is once again violating the law and disregarding a court order that clearly halted conversion of the Roxbury warehouse into a detention center,” said Governor Mikie Sherrill. “Make no mistake, this warehouse doesn’t make the community safer, isn’t fit for human habitation, and could harm the environment. This isn’t a partisan issue, and we will continue working with the Roxbury community to stop this conversion into a mass detention facility.”

“Back in May, a federal court issued an order that was crystal clear: DHS and ICE cannot take any steps to convert the Roxbury warehouse unless and until they conduct an environmental assessment. It is completely unacceptable that DHS and ICE are flouting this court order—which is why we’re going back to court today to stop their lawbreaking conduct,” said Attorney General Davenport. “As long as DHS and ICE continue to violate the law and rush this ill-conceived project, we will continue to take them to court to protect our state’s residents from their illegal overreach.”

“Roxbury Township and the New Jersey Attorney General’s Office stand united and will continue working together to protect the people, property, and resources of this community,” said Mayor Shawn Potillo. “The Council and I are extremely disappointed with the Department of Homeland Security’s lack of clear and direct communication. The information being provided has been vague, incomplete, and has failed to address the very real questions and concerns facing our community. This lack of transparency is unacceptable and places an unnecessary burden on Roxbury Township and its residents.”

In April, ICE and DHS told the court that they would not begin the process of contracting for construction work at the site until completing an environmental assessment. Based on that representation, the parties agreed to a court order in May that barred ICE from undertaking any activities to convert the warehouse into an immigration detention center until the completion of an initial environmental assessment, a final agency decision based on that assessment, and an opportunity for the State and Roxbury to challenge any decision. DHS and ICE seek to detain up to 1,500 individuals at the location.

In June, the federal government told the court that they were reassessing whether to pursue a detention center at the site at all. In status reports filed with the court in July and September, DHS and ICE claimed that they had not decided whether to pursue the warehouse and had no timetable for doing so.

However, that turned out to be false. In August, the federal government began soliciting construction bids, and received at least one bid in September. Two days after the midterm election, on November 5, they awarded a $1 billion contract to renovate the warehouse into a detention center. Of the $1 billion, $31 million is for “transition” activities, which covers potential construction of interior office space while the environmental assessment is ongoing. The contract documents also describe “transition” activities as involving renovations and the delivery of beds based on an assumption that the environmental assessment would support moving forward with a detention center—and obligates millions of dollars to this work on that basis.

As today’s motion explains, ICE has violated the court order by committing funding to begin the work of turning the industrial warehouse into a detention center before completing the required environmental assessment, and by treating the results of this environmental assessment as a forgone conclusion.

Today’s motion asks the court for an injunction barring ICE and DHS from performing or agreeing to perform any work at the site for purposes of detention center conversion. It also asks the court to direct ICE and DHS to de-obligate any federal funding committed for work at the Roxbury site, with limited exceptions. And the motion asks the court to allow the State and the Township of Roxbury to inspect the warehouse site to ensure that ICE and DHS comply with the court’s order.

The bipartisan lawsuit filed in March by Attorney General Davenport and the Township of Roxbury alleges that DHS and ICE failed to comply with federal laws requiring them to consult with state and local government officials and fully assess the project’s impacts on the environment and local resources. Roxbury is located in the Highlands region, which provides drinking water for 70% of the State of New Jersey and is designated as a “landscape of special significance” by the New Jersey Legislature.

Detaining people in an industrial warehouse not zoned for large-scale human occupancy would impose profound water and sewer burdens on Roxbury’s infrastructure and public resources, threatening public health and the local environment. If ICE and DHS attempt to draw water for the detention facility and thus further strain an already stressed water system, DHS and ICE threaten the system for the entire area. A large ongoing water withdrawal that was not previously anticipated poses a substantial risk of exceeding system capacity, which could in turn reduce water pressure and reliability for residents, impair flows needed for fighting fires, deplete groundwater, and diminish nearby wells.

###

The post AG Davenport, Roxbury Township Ask Court to Stop ICE From Violating a Court Order and Moving Forward With Warehouse Work appeared first on New Jersey Office of Attorney General.

item.title: New Jersey Division of Gaming Enforcement Announces 3rd Quarter 2026 Total Gaming Revenue Results
item.dc:creator: John Gola
item.description: The post New Jersey Division of Gaming Enforcement Announces 3rd Quarter 2026 Total Gaming Revenue Results appeared first on New Jersey Office of Attorney General.
item.content:encoded:
For Immediate Release: November 23, 2026

Office of The Attorney General
– Jennifer Davenport, Attorney General
Division of Gaming Enforcement
– Mary Jo Flaherty, Interim Director

For Further Information:

Media Inquiries-
OAGpress@njoag.gov

ATLANTIC CITY — 

Casino Net Revenue and Gross Operating Profit:

Based upon filings submitted by the casino licensees to the Division of Gaming Enforcement, 3rd Quarter 2026 Net Revenue was reported at $944.7 million, reflecting a 0.3% increase over the same quarter last year. Casino licensees reported 3rd Quarter 2026 Gross Operating Profit of $209.4 million, an 11.0% decrease compared to 3rd Quarter 2025.

For the first nine months of 2026, Net Revenue reached $2.51 billion, increasing 0.2% from the comparable period last year. For the first nine months of 2026, casino licensees reported Gross Operating Profit of $479.0 million, decreasing 13.6% compared to the same period last year.

Important information regarding the recognition of Net Revenue and Gross Operating Profit related to the Internet gaming and sports wagering business is included in the footnotes of the Quarterly Financial Report. Valid comparisons cannot be made without considering the information provided in the footnotes.

Hotel Occupancy:
The hotel occupancy rate at the casino hotels for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, was 83.7%, representing a decrease of 0.6 percentage points compared to the same quarter in 2025. The occupancy rate for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, was 74.0%, an increase of 0.7 percentage points from the comparable period last year.

Click here for the DGE press release for additional information.

item.title: Middlesex County Man Sentenced to 15 Years in Prison for Sexual Offenses in Two Counties
item.dc:creator: NJOAG Communications
item.category: nj man in prison for sexual offenses
item.description:
Attorney General Jennifer Davenport, the Division of Criminal Justice (DCJ), and the New Jersey State Police announced today that a Middlesex County man was sentenced to 15 years in state prison for the aggravated sexual assault of a 6-year-old girl in Middlesex County Superior Court, and 5 years in state prison for the possession of child sexual abuse and exploitation material (CSAEM) in Somerset County Superior Court.

The post Middlesex County Man Sentenced to 15 Years in Prison for Sexual Offenses in Two Counties appeared first on New Jersey Office of Attorney General.
item.content:encoded:
For Immediate Release: November 20, 2026

Office of The Attorney General
– Jennifer Davenport, Attorney General
Division of Criminal Justice
– Martha Nye, Interim Director
New Jersey State Police
– Jeanne Hengemuhle, Superintendent

For Further Information:

Media Inquiries-
Matthew Reilly
OAGpress@njoag.gov

TRENTON – Attorney General Jennifer Davenport, the Division of Criminal Justice (DCJ), and the New Jersey State Police announced today that a Middlesex County man was sentenced to 15 years in state prison for the aggravated sexual assault of a 6-year-old girl in Middlesex County Superior Court, and 5 years in state prison for the possession of child sexual abuse and exploitation material (CSAEM) in Somerset County Superior Court.

Shakem T. Holmes, 24, of Edison, New Jersey, previously pleaded guilty to second-degree possession of CSAEM in Somerset County, and was sentenced today by Judge Robert E. Wilson to five years in New Jersey state prison. Holmes previously pleaded guilty to first-degree aggravated sexual assault in another matter and on November 17, 2026, Superior Court Judge Andrea G. Carter Latimer in Middlesex County sentenced him to 15 years in New Jersey state prison with a 15-year parole disqualifier, pursuant to the Jessica Lunsford Act. The two sentences were ordered to run concurrently. For both criminal convictions, Holmes will be subject to parole supervision for life and required to register pursuant to Megan’s Law.

“Protecting our children is of one our highest priorities,” said Attorney General Davenport. “The conduct in this case is deeply troubling, and these sentences provide just punishment to the defendant. We will continue using every available tool we have to protect our children.”

“Our office is committed to actively investigating and prosecuting crimes committed against children,” said DCJ Interim Director Martha Nye. “The excellent work by the investigators and prosecutors in this case has resulted in a lengthy and deserved prison term for the defendant who committed offenses in multiple counties across the state.”

“The protection of children is one of our most important responsibilities,” said Jeanne Hengemuhle, Superintendent of the New Jersey State Police. “When an individual targets a child, they violate the trust and sense of security every young person deserves. This sentence reflects the gravity of that crime and demonstrates our steadfast commitment to defending those who are most vulnerable. Cases like this exemplify our detectives’ and law enforcement partners’ dedication to pursuing justice, holding offenders accountable, and preventing further harm. We will continue to work tirelessly to protect children, support victims and their families, and ensure our communities remain safe for all.”

On July 23, 2025, New Jersey State Police were contacted by a detective with the East Peoria Police Department (EPPD) in Illinois. The EPPD investigation revealed that on March 30, 2025, a 6-year-old victim was chatting with another person on a popular social media platform. The individual then began text messaging the child using a phone number later determined to be associated with Holmes. Holmes sent the victim several sexual videos of adult women, asked the victim to repeat the depicted sexual acts while recording herself and then to send the recordings to Holmes, which the victim did.

The EPPD was informed of this incident by the victim’s parents, who found the messages. After a preliminary investigation, EPPD determined the perpetrator, Holmes, was living in New Jersey and referred the case to the New Jersey State Police Internet Crimes Against Children (ICAC) Task Force. After an emergent investigation, members of the New Jersey State Police ICAC Unit executed a search warrant at a hotel where Holmes was staying and arrested Holmes. Holmes later admitted to this conduct during his guilty plea.

In October 2023, a CyberTip was received regarding potential CSAEM in a Dropbox account. This individual was later identified as Holmes, and approximately 2,000 items of CSAEM were located on his electronic devices. Holmes later admitted to this conduct during his guilty plea in Somerset County Superior Court.

The Middlesex County case was prosecuted by Deputy Attorney General Gina Imperato, and the Somerset County Case was prosecuted by Deputy Attorney General Anton Kiryako, both under the supervision of Deputy Chief Layli Khelafa.

 

Defense counsel: Elisia Tadros Esq. (Middlesex case); Christopher Rivera Esq. (Somerset case)

###

item.title: Middlesex County Man Sentenced to 90 Days in County Jail for Insurance Fraud, Attempted Theft, and Falsifying Records
item.dc:creator: NJOAG Communications
item.category: Office of the Insurance Fraud Prosecutor
item.description:
Attorney General Jennifer Davenport and the Office of the Insurance Fraud Prosecutor (OIFP) announced that a Middlesex County man was sentenced today to 90 days in county jail for submitting a fraudulent insurance claim involving damage to heavy equipment.

The post Middlesex County Man Sentenced to 90 Days in County Jail for Insurance Fraud, Attempted Theft, and Falsifying Records appeared first on New Jersey Office of Attorney General.
item.content:encoded:
For Immediate Release: November 20, 2026

Office of The Attorney General
– Jennifer Davenport, Attorney General
Office of the Insurance Fraud Prosecutor
– Bernard Cooney, Acting Insurance Fraud Prosecutor

For Further Information:

Media Inquiries-
Matthew Reilly
OAGpress@njoag.gov

TRENTON – Attorney General Jennifer Davenport and the Office of the Insurance Fraud Prosecutor (OIFP) announced that a Middlesex County man was sentenced to 90 days in county jail for submitting a fraudulent insurance claim involving damage to heavy equipment.

Andre Love, 49, of East Brunswick, was previously convicted of third-degree insurance fraud, attempted theft by deception, and fourth-degree falsifying records following a four-day trial before Superior Court Judge Robert J. Jones. Judge Jones sentenced Love today in Middlesex County to five years’ probation, conditioned upon serving 90 days in county jail, and ordered him to complete 100 hours of community service.

“The insurance system depends on all participants being honest,” said Attorney General Davenport. “Those who attempt to obtain insurance benefits through deception will be held accountable for their actions.”

“Insurance fraud can take many forms, and even a single fraudulent claim can lead to criminal prosecution,” said Acting Insurance Fraud Prosecutor Bernard Cooney. “As this case demonstrates, attempting to deceive an insurer for financial gain can result in a conviction at trial and the criminal penalties that follow.”

According to documents filed in this case and the evidence at trial, Love, the owner of Love’s Tree Removal in East Brunswick, submitted a fraudulent claim to Markel Insurance for damage to a 1995 Caterpillar Loader. Love obtained the insurance policy in September 2020 and filed a claim on May 28, 2021, claiming that an employee had damaged the loader two days earlier. On June 9, 2021, Love submitted an invoice for repairs from Monroe Repairs LLC that included a meter reading and a repair estimate of over $28,000.

Love had received an estimate for the same transmission damage to the loader in April 2020, approximately five months before applying for the policy and more than a year before filing the claim. The April 2020 estimate and the documents Love submitted in June 2021 included an identical meter reading and total work estimate. The owner of Monroe Repairs LLC confirmed that the company had neither evaluated the loader for the repairs in question nor prepared the invoice Love submitted to the insurer.

Deputy Attorneys General Jana Robinson and Vladimir D’Argenio tried the case for OIFP. The investigation was conducted by OIFP Detective Brianna Rafferty and Detective Nicholas Esposito. Analyst Bethany Schussler also assisted on the case. Acting Insurance Fraud Prosecutor Cooney thanked Markel Insurance for the referral.

OIFP’s mission includes coordination of all anti-insurance fraud activities statewide, and many successful prosecutions are a result of initial anonymous tips. If you suspect insurance fraud or have information about a potential case, OIFP wants to hear from you. You can report fraud anonymously by calling the toll-free hotline at 1-877-55-FRAUD or visiting www.NJInsurancefraud.org. State regulations permit a reward to be paid to eligible persons who provide information that leads to an arrest, prosecution, and conviction for insurance fraud.

—

Defense counsel: Thomas Belsky Esq.

###

item.title: Attorney General Davenport, Multistate Coalition Oppose CFTC Rulemakings on Gambling Products and Prediction Markets
item.dc:creator: NJOAG Communications
item.description:
Attorney General Jennifer Davenport co-led a bipartisan coalition of 44 attorneys general opposing two federal rules that would allow sports wagering, election betting, and similar gambling on prediction markets to be solely regulated by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), overriding states’ traditional authority in this area.

The post Attorney General Davenport, Multistate Coalition Oppose CFTC Rulemakings on Gambling Products and Prediction Markets appeared first on New Jersey Office of Attorney General.
item.content:encoded:
Bipartisan Coalition Defends States’ Traditional Authority to Regulate Gambling

For Immediate Release: November 20, 2026

Office of The Attorney General
– Jennifer Davenport, Attorney General

For Further Information:

Media Inquiries-
Allison Inserro
OAGpress@njoag.gov

View Swaps Comment Letter | View IFR Comment Letter

TRENTON — Attorney General Jennifer Davenport co-led a bipartisan coalition of 44 attorneys general opposing two federal rules that would allow sports wagering, election betting, and similar gambling on prediction markets to be solely regulated by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), overriding states’ traditional authority in this area.

“The CFTC continues to stray far outside of its lane by seeking to exclusively regulate certain forms of sports gambling on prediction markets,” said Attorney General Davenport. “These actions seek to override states’ longstanding authority to regulate gambling within our borders, which would allow prediction markets to operate without complying with state gambling regulations and safeguards to ensure responsible gaming.”

Prediction markets, such as Kalshi and Polymarket, allow users to place wagers on game winners, point spreads, and player statistics. Prediction markets claim that they are operating as contract markets regulated by the CFTC, and that they are therefore exempt from the regulations and protections imposed by state gambling laws.

The CFTC is the federal agency that oversees financial markets where traders buy and sell contracts tied to the future price of things like oil, wheat, interest rates, or foreign currency. This includes certain “swaps,” which are deals where two parties agree to exchange payments based on how something changes in value, such as an interest rate or a currency. The CFTC has not traditionally regulated gambling or other contracts used for entertainment rather than financial risk management.

Both CFTC rules seek to change what counts as a “swap” under federal law. The first rule, which is an interim rule currently in effect, distinguishes between “casino style” games backed by a “house” and games where bettors wager against each other. Under the interim rule, only house-backed “casino style” games are considered traditional gambling products and, therefore, are not “swaps.” The second rule is a proposal, not yet in effect, that expands the definition of “swap” to include things like sports and election betting where bettors wager against each other. Because they would be considered “swaps,” they would be regulated by the CFTC, which has argued that it displaces states’ control over such gambling.

In comment letters filed this week, the multistate coalition voiced objections to the CFTC rules. The coalition’s position is that the regulation of gambling and protection of residents from associated harms falls within the states’ traditional police powers over gambling; that the CFTC regulates specific financial markets and has no legal power to address the harms that gambling can cause; and that the CFTC skipped required steps in writing these rules and went beyond the rulemaking power Congress gave it.

New Jersey has asked the U.S. Supreme Court to hear its case against the prediction market Kalshi, with the support of 39 states and the District of Columbia, along with 146 tribal nations and tribal organizations. The majority of federal courts across the country to have addressed these issues have rejected the conclusion that prediction markets allowing sports betting are exempt from state law.

Joining Attorney General Davenport in the coalition opposing the CFTC rules are the attorneys general of Alabama, Alaska, Arizona, Arkansas, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Delaware, the District of Columbia, Hawaii, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, Mississippi, Nebraska, Nevada, New Mexico, New York, North Carolina, Ohio, Oklahoma, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, South Carolina, South Dakota, Tennessee, Utah, Vermont, Virginia, and Wisconsin.

###

item.title: NJ Bureau of Securities Sues Gloucester County Couple in Alleged $1.5 Million Real Estate Investment Scheme Tied to Social Media
item.dc:creator: NJOAG Communications
item.description:
Attorney General Jennifer Davenport announced today that the New Jersey Bureau of Securities (Bureau) has filed a civil enforcement action against a social media influencer couple from Swedesboro who allegedly used their platform to pose as successful real estate investors, luring followers into a more than $1.5 million Ponzi-like investment scam.

The post NJ Bureau of Securities Sues Gloucester County Couple in Alleged $1.5 Million Real Estate Investment Scheme Tied to Social Media appeared first on New Jersey Office of Attorney General.
item.content:encoded:
For Immediate Release: November 20, 2026

Office of The Attorney General
– Jennifer Davenport, Attorney General
Division of Consumer Affairs
– Christopher Peterson, Acting Director
Bureau of Securities
– Keith A. Alt, Acting Bureau Chief
Division of Law
– Michael Walters, Director

 

For Further Information:

Media Inquiries-
Lisa Coryell 
OAGpress@njoag.gov

View Complaint

TRENTON – Attorney General Jennifer Davenport announced today that the New Jersey Bureau of Securities (Bureau) has filed a civil enforcement action against a social media influencer couple from Swedesboro who allegedly used their platform to pose as successful real estate investors, luring followers into a more than $1.5 million Ponzi-like investment scam.

Gregory Dorell Parker Jr. and his wife, Danielle “Nikki” Morris Parker, who projected an image of jet-setting wealth through their Big Bizzneesss, Diamante Financing, and other social media brands, allegedly defrauded more than 30 investors––including at least nine in New Jersey­––who put money into bogus real estate projects the Parkers claimed to be developing.

In a complaint filed in Superior Court in Gloucester County, the Bureau alleges the Parkers and their associated brands violated New Jersey’s Uniform Securities Act through the sale of unregistered securities and other unlawful conduct tied to the scheme.

“New Jersey investors deserve a fair and honest marketplace where they can put their money to work and build wealth,” said Attorney General Davenport. “We will continue pursuing investment scammers and holding them accountable to protect people’s hard-earned savings.”

“As we allege in our complaint, the Parkers ran a multi-year, Ponzi-like scheme targeting followers who believed in them and the real estate projects they claimed to be working on,” said Christopher Peterson, Acting Director of the Division of Consumer Affairs. “Our lawsuit seeks to recover investors’ money and hold the Parkers accountable for their unlawful conduct.”

“This case exposes how scammers use the internet to project false images of wealth and success, then convince investors to hand over their money in hopes of achieving the same,” said Keith A. Alt, Acting Bureau Chief. “We urge investors to research both the investment offered and the people offering it, and to contact the Bureau to check their registration status, before investing.”

According to the Bureau’s complaint, the Parkers solicited the investors through social media campaigns, mutual contacts in the community, and a recurring pipeline of paid seminars, mentorship programs, and investor events, all of which they used to project an image of success in the real estate business and to channel attendees into their real estate investment scheme.

The Parkers allegedly represented to investors that their money would fund the purchase or renovation of specific properties the Parkers or their companies owned or would acquire, that investors would see returns on their investments within a set timeframe or upon the Parkers’ successful completion of the projects or delivery of property, and that the Parkers and their associates would handle all the work.

The Bureau alleges that the properties in reality were unsuitable for the promised renovations, that often neither the Parkers nor their companies owned them, and that investor funds were not used to purchase them. The Bureau further alleges the investments could not generate the promised returns, and the Parkers cut off or sharply reduced contact with investors after receiving their money, taking no steps to advance the projects.

Additionally, the Bureau alleges the Parkers failed to disclose to investors that their companies had no legitimate revenue to pay the promised returns, their home had been subject to foreclosure proceedings, Gregory Parker had filed for personal bankruptcy in 2018, and neither they nor the investments were registered with the Bureau or exempt from registration. According to the complaint, they also concealed that investor funds would be mixed with other money, moved through dozens of accounts and entities to obscure their trail, and used for personal expenses and payments to earlier investors.

The six-count complaint alleges securities fraud, the sale of unregistered securities, and violations involving unregistered agents.  The following entities created, operated, and owned by Greg Parker and/or Danielle Morris Parker are also named as defendants: Big Bizzneesss, LLC; Diamante Enterprises LLC; Diamante Financing, LLC; and AP Capital LLC.  The complaint seeks civil monetary penalties, restitution, and the return of profits or funds obtained through alleged violations of New Jersey’s Uniform Securities Act. It also seeks to bar the defendants from offering or selling securities from, into, or within New Jersey and from controlling an issuer, broker-dealer, or investment adviser.

The Bureau filed its Complaint against the Parkers and the named Parker entities in tandem with the Pennsylvania Department of Banking and Securities, which ordered the Parkers and the Parkers’ Big Bizzneesss, LLC, Diamante Investment Group, LLC, Diamante Financing, LLC, and Diamante Enterprises, LLC entities to cease and desist from offering and selling unregistered securities in violation of the Pennsylvania Securities Act of 1972.

The Bureau is charged with protecting investors from investment fraud and regulating the securities industry in New Jersey.

The Bureau’s investigation was handled by Investigators Eugene Kizenko, Isaac Reyes, Marc N. Kollie, and Boris V. Maltsev, under the supervision of Supervising Investigators Sharon B. MacDermott and Myles L. Orosco, and Regulatory Chief Rachel D. Glasgow.  Deputy Attorney General Hovhannes Onno Chekemian of the Securities Fraud Prosecution Section in the Division of Law’s Affirmative Civil Enforcement Practice Group is representing the Bureau in this matter, under the supervision of Deputy Attorney General Evan A. Showell, Assistant Section Chief of the Securities Fraud Prosecution Section, and Assistant Attorney General Brian F. McDonough.

It is critical that investors “Check Before You Invest.”  Investors can obtain information, including the registration status and disciplinary history, of any financial professional doing business to or from New Jersey, by contacting the Bureau toll-free within New Jersey at 1-866-I-Invest (1-866-446-8378) or from outside New Jersey at (973) 504-3600, or by visiting the Bureau’s website at www.NJSecurities.gov.  Investors can also contact the Bureau for assistance, or to raise issues or complaints about New Jersey-based financial professionals or investments.

item.title: New Jersey Division of Consumer Affairs Launches Modernized Website to Improve User Experience
item.dc:creator: NJOAG Communications WC
item.description:
Attorney General Jennifer Davenport and the Division of Consumer Affairs announced the launch of the Division’s redesigned website, offering New Jersey consumers, licensed professionals, businesses, and other visitors a more accessible, intuitive, and user-friendly online experience.

The post New Jersey Division of Consumer Affairs Launches Modernized Website to Improve User Experience appeared first on New Jersey Office of Attorney General.
item.content:encoded:
For Immediate Release: November 19, 2026

Office of the Attorney General
– Jennifer Davenport, Attorney General
Division of Consumer Affairs
– Christopher Peterson, Acting Director

For Further Information:

Media Inquiries-
Lisa Coryell
OAGpress@njoag.gov

TRENTON – Attorney General Jennifer Davenport and the Division of Consumer Affairs (Division) today announced the launch of the Division’s redesigned website, offering New Jersey consumers, licensed professionals, businesses, and other visitors a more accessible, intuitive, and user-friendly online experience.

The modernized website features a streamlined design and improved navigation that make it easier for consumers to find important information about their rights and protections while helping licensed professionals, registrants, and businesses access the resources they need to understand and meet their regulatory obligations.

“Getting the information and resources you need from state government should be simple and straightforward,” said Attorney General Davenport. “Whether you’re a consumer seeking to protect yourself from fraud or a licensed professional or business working to meet your legal obligations, our updated website makes it easier to find what you’re looking for.”

“Our website is one of the most important ways we connect with the public we serve and the professionals and businesses we regulate,” said Christopher Peterson, Acting Director of the Division of Consumer Affairs. “The redesigned site reflects our commitment to making those interactions easier and more productive by simplifying access to consumer protection resources and providing clearer pathways to licensing and regulatory information.”

A key feature of the redesigned website is the addition of two distinct navigation options for consumers and for professionals that provide visitors with quick, direct access to the information and resources most relevant to their needs.

The revamped online platform also supports the Division’s mission of promoting compliance with the laws and regulations governing licensed professionals and regulated businesses in New Jersey. A new “Guidance Circulars” section, accessible through the “Resources” tab on the homepage, serves as a central repository for official directives, policy instructions, and notices issued by the Division and its licensing boards to announce regulatory requirements and clarify laws and rules for consumers, licensees, businesses, and other stakeholders.

Additionally, the updated website provides greater transparency into the Division’s structure and operations, featuring a new organizational chart outlining its offices, units, and licensing boards; a leadership page identifying key personnel and their responsibilities; and a searchable press release archive that allows visitors to find announcements by subject.

The revamped website is available at https://dca.njoag.gov/

###

item.title: Attorney General Davenport, Alcoholic Beverage Control Launch Interactive Dashboard Detailing Alcohol Licenses Across New Jersey
item.dc:creator: NJOAG Communications
item.description:
Attorney General Jennifer Davenport, the Division of Alcoholic Beverage Control (ABC), and the Office of Justice Data (OJD) announced new actions to improve information sharing and increase transparency about alcoholic beverage control licenses.

The post Attorney General Davenport, Alcoholic Beverage Control Launch Interactive Dashboard Detailing Alcohol Licenses Across New Jersey appeared first on New Jersey Office of Attorney General.
item.content:encoded:
ABC Also Updates Its Handbook

For Immediate Release: November 18, 2026

Office of The Attorney General
– Jennifer Davenport, Attorney General
Division of Alcoholic Beverage Control
– Paul Urbish, Acting Director
Office of Justice Data
– Kristin Golden, PhD, Chief Data Officer

 

For Further Information:

Media Inquiries-
Allison Inserro
OAGpress@njoag.gov

TRENTON – Attorney General Jennifer Davenport, the Division of Alcoholic Beverage Control (ABC), and the Office of Justice Data (OJD) announced new actions to improve information sharing and increase transparency about alcoholic beverage control licenses.

First, information about all state-issued and retail alcoholic beverage control licenses can now be found in a new interactive, graphical dashboard. The ABC Licensee Dashboard pulls publicly available information about different types of licenses and displays an interactive map that lets users examine data at the county and municipal level. This is the thirteenth dashboard released by OJD since the office was created in 2021.

Second, ABC announced that an updated Retail Licensees Handbook is now available. It is the first update of the handbook since New Jersey began updating and streamlining the State’s alcoholic beverage control laws.

“Many New Jersey residents are interested in who owns alcoholic beverage licenses and where they are located. Data visualization opens a window into government and gives the public a clear way to view important information,” said Attorney General Davenport. “My office is proud to bring more transparency to the Garden State.”

“Public visibility of alcohol license types and locations strengthens trust in government by showing that regulations are not hidden—they’re shared openly with the people they serve,” said Paul Urbish, Acting Director of the ABC.

“Making licensing information public transforms a complex regulatory system into an accessible resource for the community,” said Dr. Kristin Golden, OJD Chief Data Officer.

Data in the dashboard will be updated monthly. The dashboard allows sorting by county, municipality, and licenses by type using colorful icons. Hovering over a license displays a pop-up box with the name of the license holder, license number, and other information.

Both the dashboard and the handbook are for general informational purposes only. In the case of the dashboard, licensees are encouraged to use the online POSSE system or contact ABC directly to ensure the most up-to-date information. The handbook is intended as a reference tool, and if there is a conflict between the handbook and applicable law or regulation, the law or regulation applies.

###

item.title: New Jersey Division of Gaming Enforcement Announces October 2026 Total Gaming Revenue Results
item.dc:creator: John Gola
item.description:
Today the New Jersey Division of Gaming Enforcement announced the July 2026 total gaming revenue results.

The post New Jersey Division of Gaming Enforcement Announces October 2026 Total Gaming Revenue Results appeared first on New Jersey Office of Attorney General.
item.content:encoded:
For Immediate Release: November 17, 2026

Office of The Attorney General
– Jennifer Davenport, Attorney General
Division of Gaming Enforcement
– Mary Jo Flaherty, Interim Director

For Further Information:

Media Inquiries-
OAGpress@njoag.gov

ATLANTIC CITY — Today the New Jersey Division of Gaming Enforcement announced the October 2026 total gaming revenue results.

Casino Win:
Casino Win for the nine casino hotels was $245.9 million for October 2026, reflecting an increase of 4.7% when compared to $234.7 million reported for October 2025. Year-to-date Casino Win was $2.48 billion through October 2026, reflecting an increase of 1.8% compared to the prior year-to-date period. The Monthly Gross Revenue Reports are posted online at https://www.njoag.gov/about/divisions-and-offices/division-of-gaming-enforcement-home/financial-and-statistical-information/monthly-gross-revenue-reports/

Internet Gaming Win:
Internet Gaming Win for the casinos and their partners was $287.4 million for October 2026, reflecting growth of 10.4% when compared to $260.3 million reported for October 2025. Year-to-date Internet Gaming Win was $2.69 billion through October 2026, reflecting growth of 12.9% when compared to $2.39 billion for the prior year-to-date period. The Monthly Internet Gaming Gross Revenue Reports are posted online at https://www.njoag.gov/about/divisions-and-offices/division-of-gaming-enforcement-home/financial-and-statistical-information/monthly-internet-gross-revenue-reports/

Sports Wagering Gross Revenue:
Sports Wagering Gross Revenue for the casinos, racetracks, and their partners was $116.3 million for October 2026, reflecting an increase of 0.2% when compared to $116.1 million reported for October 2025. Year-to-date Sports Wagering Gross Revenue was $864.6 million through October 2026, reflecting a decrease of 5.5% when compared to $914.6 million reported for the prior year-to-date period. The Monthly Sports Wagering Tax Returns are posted online at https://www.njoag.gov/about/divisions-and-offices/division-of-gaming-enforcement-home/financial-and-statistical-information/monthly-sports-wagering-revenue-reports/

Total Gaming Revenue:
Total Gaming Revenue for casinos, racetracks, and their partners was $649.5 million for October 2026, reflecting an increase of 6.3% when compared to $611.1 million reported for October 2025. Year-to-date Total Gaming Revenue was $6.04 billion through October 2026, reflecting 5.2% growth when compared to $5.74 billion reported for the prior year-to-date period. Total Gross Revenue Taxes were $94.3 million for October 2026 and $851.1 million for year-to-date through October 2026.
